providers.name: VidLux
providers.note: Fastest to a stream of anything measured — 1.4s. Keys on TMDB ids rather than IMDB, so it works for titles TMDB has and IMDB search found.

providers.name: VidFast
providers.note: Served every canary and the quickest to start — 1.3s. Moved here from vidfast.pro, which still redirects; pointing straight at the new domain measured 500ms faster because it skips that hop.

providers.name: VidFlix
providers.note: Played the right title and episode on every content check, anime included. Serves the VidSpark player, the same backend as VidSrc PM. Its landing page is a 655-byte shell, which looks broken to anything that only checks the document.

providers.name: CinemaOS
providers.note: Served every canary, but slowest to start — around 3.7s. TMDB-keyed.

providers.name: ScreenScape
providers.note: Played the right title and episode on every content check, anime included. Asks for English audio explicitly: without lan=eng it picks a Hindi dub whenever one exists. Season and episode must be s= and e= — season= and episode= are silently ignored.

providers.name: MoviesAPI
providers.note: Thin catalogue — served one canary of four, and its API 404s for titles it lacks. Kept because when it has something it is the quickest to start.

providers.name: SuperEmbed
providers.note: Streamed 1 of 8 canary attempts across two runs, and took 6.5s when it worked. Kept as opt-in rather than removed because it does sometimes serve titles nothing else has; the reliability ranking will sink it on its own.

providers.name: VidSrc
providers.note: Restored after being wrongly deleted. Its page vendors disable-devtool wired to a handler that pauses the video, strips its src and navigates away when it thinks a devtools panel is open — so an automated probe always records 'nothing played' no matter how long it waits. Serves a full 54KB player to an ordinary request.

providers.name: VidSrc (.sh)
providers.note: The same player as vidsrcme.ru, byte for byte, on the domain the family now calls its main one — vidsrcme.su redirects here. Played the right title and episode on every content check, anime included. A spare door onto the VidSrc backend rather than a second source.

providers.name: VidSrc PM
providers.note: Not part of the VidSrc family despite the name: it serves the VidSpark player, the same one as VidFlix, down to identical stream lengths. Needs TMDB ids — an IMDB id on a series reaches its backend as a TMDB id and finds nothing. Films and series play; anime did not.

providers.name: Videasy
providers.note: Verified streaming. Redirects from player.videasy.net, so the catalogue names the destination directly. Shares the peakstorm.top backend with VidCore.

providers.name: VidCore
providers.note: Verified streaming in 3.8s. Same peakstorm.top backend as Videasy, so it is a spare address rather than a second source.

providers.name: VidZee
providers.note: Verified streaming. Keys on TMDB ids, so it covers titles with no IMDB id.

providers.name: 111Movies
providers.note: Played the right title and episode on every content check, anime included, and names both in its own controls. Its player lives under /embed/; the bare /movie/ and /tv/ paths are its "Video Not Found" page. TMDB ids only — an IMDB id on a series is rejected.
